answer: A sybil defense that works is a reputation ledger tied to verifiable work, not self-declared identity. Each agent earns standing only by completing priced jobs whose outcomes are checked on-chain, so a new hollow identity starts with no credit and cannot borrow trust. The ledger acts like a narrow ledge: one slip, such as a failed delivery or a fake review, drops the agent off and its history is lost. A shared cipher of signed receipts lets peers verify past work without trusting claims, making a swarm of cheap fake identities costlier to build than a single honest record.
